For notices served 3/01/26–2/28/27, the amount is $446 per day per tenant household plus actual moving expenses. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9.

Lower-income households (80% AMI or below) displaced by demolition of their units for replacement with new construction must receive relocation benefits consistent with those public entities must pay under Government Code Section 7260 et seq. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 66300.6(b)(4)(A).
Coverage depends on government subsidized, owner is corporation, owner occupied, which the public records do not include. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12.

Landlords may not use the credit history of an applicant who has a government rental subsidy, such as Section 8, unless they offer the applicant the option to provide alternative evidence of a verifiable lawful means to pay their portion of the rent. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955 (SB 267).

Housing providers may check criminal history but may not consider arrests that did not lead to a conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and may not have blanket bans on people with criminal history. A denial based on a conviction must be directly related to tenancy and safety, considering the nature and severity of the crime and the time passed. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA), Cal. Gov. Code § 12900 et seq..

Housing providers may not discriminate against applicants or tenants based on how they will pay rent (source of income). This includes Housing Choice (Section 8) vouchers and other rental assistance. Providers may not refuse to comply with subsidy program requirements, apply different terms such as higher deposits, or advertise 'No Section 8.' Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA), Cal. Gov. Code § 12900 et seq..

A landlord may not demand or receive security, however named, of more than one month's rent on top of the first month's rent. Small landlords who are natural persons (or LLCs of natural persons) owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units in total may charge up to two months' rent, except to service members. The landlord must return the deposit with an itemized statement within 21 days after move-out, and may not call any part of it nonrefundable. The section was last amended by AB 414 (Stats. 2025, Ch. 340), effective January 1, 2026. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5.

Bans selling or using algorithmic devices that analyze nonpublic competitor rental data to recommend rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco. A tenant or the City Attorney may sue a violator. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.10C.

A landlord may evict a tenant from a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance only for one of 17 listed just cause reasons, and that reason must be the dominant motive for the eviction. The end of a lease or a change in ownership alone is not just cause. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9(a).

Landlords who evict tenants under the Ellis Act (withdrawal of units from the rental market) must pay relocation. For notices served 3/01/26 to 2/28/27 it is $11,110.05 per tenant, up to $33,330.13 per unit, plus $7,443.90 for each elderly (62+) or disabled tenant. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9A(e).

Landlords who evict for owner/relative move-in, demolition or permanent removal from housing use, temporary capital improvement work, or substantial rehabilitation must pay relocation. The amount depends on the date the eviction notice is served. For notices served 3/01/26 to 2/28/27 it is $8,245.00 per tenant, up to $24,733.00 per unit, plus $5,497.00 for each elderly (60+) or disabled tenant or household with minor children. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9C.

For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable rent increase effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6% of the tenant's base rent. The prior period's (March 1, 2025 to February 28, 2026) allowable increase was 1.4%. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code ch. 37 (Residential Rent Stabilization and Arbitration Ordinance), annual allowable increase.
Coverage depends on government subsidized, which the public records do not include. Source: San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

Landlords must pay interest on security deposits at the Rent Board rate of 4.2% for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027. Earlier periods used 5.0% (2025–26) and 5.2% (2024–25). Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code Ch. 49 (Security Deposit Interest).

A0034.explanation: Proposed, not law. Would cover this building if enacted. Source: Cambridge City Council policy order (number not stated).

Landlords, sellers and rental agents may not discriminate in renting housing, including viewing, renting and the terms of tenancy, based on protected categories. These include source of income (including Section 8 and public benefits), race, disability, family status and others. Landlords may use any reasonable selection standard, such as ability to pay rent, if it is applied equally and uniformly to all applicants. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cambridge Mun. Code ch. 14.04 (Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance).

Only licensed brokers may charge prospective tenants fees for finding housing, and the broker must give the applicant written notice of the fee amount, time and manner of payment, and whether it depends on a lease being signed, at the first personal meeting. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: 254 CMR 7.

At or before the start of a tenancy, a landlord or the landlord's agent may not require a tenant or applicant to pay the landlord or its agent anything beyond first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit of up to one month's rent, and the cost of buying and installing a key and lock. The 2025 amendment, effective August 1, 2025, extended the limit to the lessor's agents and payments to them; earlier text applied only to lessors. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(1)(b), as amended by St. 2025, c. 9, §§ 54-55.

A real estate broker or salesperson may contract only with the prospective tenant or only with the landlord (or landlord's agent), and any fee may be paid only by the party who originally hired the broker. Landlords cannot pass the fee of a broker they hired on to tenants. Only licensed brokers or salespersons may charge a fee for finding rental housing. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 112, § 87DDD½ (as amended by St. 2025, c. 9, § 43).

Either party may end a tenancy at will with written notice of three months, or, if rent is paid more often than every three months, notice equal to the rental period or 30 days, whichever is longer; no reason for ending the tenancy is required. For nonpayment of rent, a landlord may end the tenancy with a 14-day written notice to quit, but a tenant who has not received such a notice in the prior 12 months can stop the termination by paying all rent due within 10 days. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 186, § 12.

A written notice to quit for nonpayment of rent to a residential tenant must come with a state form. The form must document any repayment agreements, give information on rental assistance, court rules and legal limits on evictions, and prominently state that the notice is not an eviction. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 31.

Anyone offering rental housing may not discriminate against a person because they receive public assistance or a housing subsidy, such as a rental voucher, or because of any requirement of that assistance or subsidy program. Ads for covered rental housing also may not state a preference or limit based on public assistance recipiency. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 151B, § 4(10).

A landlord may not require a security deposit greater than the first month's rent. The deposit must be held in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account, receipted, accompanied by a statement of condition, earn interest for the tenant, and be returned (less lawful itemized deductions) within 30 days after the tenancy ends. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B.

A0035.explanation: No person may use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (software or other method used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set or influence a price or commercial term) as part of a contract, combination or conspiracy to restrain trade. No person may use or distribute such an algorithm while coercing another person to adopt its recommended price or terms. The law covers all products and services, not only rental housing. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729.

A landlord may charge a rental applicant a screening fee no greater than actual out-of-pocket screening costs, and never more than $30 per applicant (adjustable annually by CPI since January 1, 1998). The landlord may collect the fee only when a unit is or will soon be available and only if it offers either a first-come, first-qualified screening process or a full refund to applicants not selected. The landlord must also give an itemized receipt, return unused amounts and provide a copy of the credit report. The current text reflects the amendment by Stats. 2025, Ch. 67 (AB 1170), effective January 1, 2026. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6.

Owners who demolish a Protected Unit for new construction must pay relocation under one of three options, paying the higher of State (Housing Crisis Act) or City amounts. Lower-income households receive enhanced standardized payments; all tenants receive at least RSO or JCO amounts within 15 days. Tenants also get rights to remain up to 6 months before construction, to return if demolition does not proceed, and in some cases a right of first refusal. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: L.A. Ordinance Nos. 188481 and 188482 (Resident Protections Ordinance).

Source: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (L.A. Mun. Code).

Source: Boston Housing Stability Notification Act, City of Boston Ordinances Sec. 10-11.7.

Only licensed brokers may charge prospective tenants fees for finding housing, and the broker must give the applicant written notice of the fee amount, time and manner of payment, and whether it depends on a lease being signed, at the first personal meeting. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: 254 CMR 7.

At or before the start of a tenancy, a landlord or the landlord's agent may not require a tenant or applicant to pay the landlord or its agent anything beyond first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit of up to one month's rent, and the cost of buying and installing a key and lock. The 2025 amendment, effective August 1, 2025, extended the limit to the lessor's agents and payments to them; earlier text applied only to lessors. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(1)(b), as amended by St. 2025, c. 9, §§ 54-55.

A real estate broker or salesperson may contract only with the prospective tenant or only with the landlord (or landlord's agent), and any fee may be paid only by the party who originally hired the broker. Landlords cannot pass the fee of a broker they hired on to tenants. Only licensed brokers or salespersons may charge a fee for finding rental housing. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 112, § 87DDD½ (as amended by St. 2025, c. 9, § 43).

Either party may end a tenancy at will with written notice of three months, or, if rent is paid more often than every three months, notice equal to the rental period or 30 days, whichever is longer; no reason for ending the tenancy is required. For nonpayment of rent, a landlord may end the tenancy with a 14-day written notice to quit, but a tenant who has not received such a notice in the prior 12 months can stop the termination by paying all rent due within 10 days. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 186, § 12.

A written notice to quit for nonpayment of rent to a residential tenant must come with a state form. The form must document any repayment agreements, give information on rental assistance, court rules and legal limits on evictions, and prominently state that the notice is not an eviction. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 31.

Anyone offering rental housing may not discriminate against a person because they receive public assistance or a housing subsidy, such as a rental voucher, or because of any requirement of that assistance or subsidy program. Ads for covered rental housing also may not state a preference or limit based on public assistance recipiency. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 151B, § 4(10).

A landlord may not require a security deposit greater than the first month's rent. The deposit must be held in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account, receipted, accompanied by a statement of condition, earn interest for the tenant, and be returned (less lawful itemized deductions) within 30 days after the tenancy ends. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B.

A0040.explanation: Landlords renting any residential dwelling unit in Hoboken may not use software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms that collect and analyze nonpublic competitor information to coordinate, recommend or implement rents, lease terms or occupancy levels among competing lessors. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Hoboken City Code § 158-2 (Ord. No. B-781).

This is not a cap on rent increases. A landlord who raises rent by more than 10% year over year on a lease renewal with a current tenant must first give certain disclosures, either on the first page of the renewal lease or on a Division of Housing form. The disclosures are an itemization of the costs behind the increase, whether a rent algorithm was used, the tenant's right to sue over an unconscionable or unlawful increase, and Division of Housing contact information. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Hoboken City Code § 158-1 (Ord. No. B-750).

Rents in covered Hoboken dwellings are controlled at the October 1, 1985 base rent level. At lease expiration or termination of a periodic tenancy, a landlord may not request or receive an increase greater than 5% or the CPI change, whichever is less, and no more than one such increase is allowed in any 12-month period. Increases above this are void. Separate Board-approved surcharges (tax, water/sewer, capital improvement) and hardship increases are allowed. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Hoboken City Code §§ 155-3, 155-4, 155-5.
Coverage depends on year built, which the public records do not include. Source: Hoboken City Code §§ 155-31 to 155-34.

A landlord or its agent may not charge an application or similar fee above $50 to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental unit. Starting January 1 of the year after enactment, the cap is adjusted each year for inflation (CPI-U, NY-Northern NJ-Long Island) and published by the Division of Consumer Affairs. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-18.1 (P.L. 2025, c.405).

A residential landlord may not evict a tenant, or refuse to renew a written or oral lease, without one of the statutory good causes. Each cause, except nonpayment of rent, requires a written Notice to Quit. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1.

There is no state rent cap, but a rent increase must not be unconscionable and must follow any municipal rent ordinance. Rent cannot be raised mid-lease; a tenant can be evicted for not paying an increase only after a valid notice to quit and notice of rent increase. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(f).
Coverage depends on year built, which the public records do not include. Source: N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5.

Housing providers may not ask about an applicant's criminal record, orally, in writing or on an application, until after making a conditional offer. They may never consider arrests without conviction, expunged, pardoned, vacated, juvenile or sealed records. After the offer they may consider only listed serious convictions and convictions within look-back periods (6 years first degree, 4 years second/third degree, 1 year fourth degree). They may withdraw an offer only after an individualized assessment showing a substantial, legitimate, nondiscriminatory interest, with written reasons and a chance to appeal. The act also bars requiring drug or alcohol tests. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-52 to 46:8-64 (P.L. 2021, c.110).

Landlords may not discriminate in housing based on the source of lawful income or the source of lawful rent payment a tenant uses. For example, a landlord cannot deny a Section 8 voucher holder an apartment based solely on that source of income. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: New Jersey Law Against Discrimination, N.J.S.A. 10:5-1 et seq..

A landlord may not collect a security deposit greater than one and one-half times one month's rent. Prepaid rent, including last month's rent, counts toward this limit. The deposit must be returned with interest, less itemized deductions, within 30 days after the tenancy ends. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2.

The act this section belongs to (L.1967, c. 265) applies to all rental premises or units used as dwellings. The one exception is owner-occupied premises with no more than two rental units, and only where the tenant has not given the landlord 30 days' written notice invoking the act. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-26.

A0041.explanation: No person may use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (software or other method used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set or influence a price or commercial term) as part of a contract, combination or conspiracy to restrain trade. No person may use or distribute such an algorithm while coercing another person to adopt its recommended price or terms. The law covers all products and services, not only rental housing. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729.

A landlord may charge a rental applicant a screening fee no greater than actual out-of-pocket screening costs, and never more than $30 per applicant (adjustable annually by CPI since January 1, 1998). The landlord may collect the fee only when a unit is or will soon be available and only if it offers either a first-come, first-qualified screening process or a full refund to applicants not selected. The landlord must also give an itemized receipt, return unused amounts and provide a copy of the credit report. The current text reflects the amendment by Stats. 2025, Ch. 67 (AB 1170), effective January 1, 2026. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6.
Coverage depends on tenancy months, owner occupied, owner is corporation, government subsidized, which the public records do not include. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2.

For temporary capital improvement evictions lasting less than 20 days, relocation payments are governed by California Civil Code Section 1947.9 rather than the San Francisco Rent Ordinance. For notices served 3/01/26–2/28/27, the amount is $446 per day per tenant household plus actual moving expenses. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9.

Lower-income households (80% AMI or below) displaced by demolition of their units for replacement with new construction must receive relocation benefits consistent with those public entities must pay under Government Code Section 7260 et seq. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 66300.6(b)(4)(A).
Coverage depends on government subsidized, owner is corporation, owner occupied, which the public records do not include. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12.

Landlords may not use the credit history of an applicant who has a government rental subsidy, such as Section 8, unless they offer the applicant the option to provide alternative evidence of a verifiable lawful means to pay their portion of the rent. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955 (SB 267).

Housing providers may check criminal history but may not consider arrests that did not lead to a conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and may not have blanket bans on people with criminal history. A denial based on a conviction must be directly related to tenancy and safety, considering the nature and severity of the crime and the time passed. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA), Cal. Gov. Code § 12900 et seq..

Housing providers may not discriminate against applicants or tenants based on how they will pay rent (source of income). This includes Housing Choice (Section 8) vouchers and other rental assistance. Providers may not refuse to comply with subsidy program requirements, apply different terms such as higher deposits, or advertise 'No Section 8.' Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA), Cal. Gov. Code § 12900 et seq..

A landlord may not demand or receive security, however named, of more than one month's rent on top of the first month's rent. Small landlords who are natural persons (or LLCs of natural persons) owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units in total may charge up to two months' rent, except to service members. The landlord must return the deposit with an itemized statement within 21 days after move-out, and may not call any part of it nonrefundable. The section was last amended by AB 414 (Stats. 2025, Ch. 340), effective January 1, 2026. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5.

Bans selling or using algorithmic devices that analyze nonpublic competitor rental data to recommend rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco. A tenant or the City Attorney may sue a violator. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.10C.

A landlord may evict a tenant from a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance only for one of 17 listed just cause reasons, and that reason must be the dominant motive for the eviction. The end of a lease or a change in ownership alone is not just cause. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9(a).

Landlords who evict tenants under the Ellis Act (withdrawal of units from the rental market) must pay relocation. For notices served 3/01/26 to 2/28/27 it is $11,110.05 per tenant, up to $33,330.13 per unit, plus $7,443.90 for each elderly (62+) or disabled tenant. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9A(e).

Landlords who evict for owner/relative move-in, demolition or permanent removal from housing use, temporary capital improvement work, or substantial rehabilitation must pay relocation. The amount depends on the date the eviction notice is served. For notices served 3/01/26 to 2/28/27 it is $8,245.00 per tenant, up to $24,733.00 per unit, plus $5,497.00 for each elderly (60+) or disabled tenant or household with minor children. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9C.

For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable rent increase effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6% of the tenant's base rent. The prior period's (March 1, 2025 to February 28, 2026) allowable increase was 1.4%. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code ch. 37 (Residential Rent Stabilization and Arbitration Ordinance), annual allowable increase.
Coverage depends on government subsidized, which the public records do not include. Source: San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

Landlords must pay interest on security deposits at the Rent Board rate of 4.2% for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027. Earlier periods used 5.0% (2025–26) and 5.2% (2024–25). Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code Ch. 49 (Security Deposit Interest).

A0042.explanation: Landlords may not use algorithmic rent coordination services. The ban is enforced both by the city and through private lawsuits. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Jersey City Code § 218-12.

Jersey City regulates rent increases under its Rent Control Ordinance, which the Office of Landlord/Tenant Relations administers and enforces. Properties with 1 to 4 units are exempt. Landlords seeking increases beyond the regulated amount must apply, for example for capital improvements or hardship. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Jersey City Mun. Code Ch. 260.

Landlords may use any reasonable selection standard, such as ability to pay rent, if it is applied equally and uniformly to all applicants. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cambridge Mun. Code ch. 14.04 (Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance).

Owners who demolish a Protected Unit for new construction must pay relocation under one of three options, paying the higher of State (Housing Crisis Act) or City amounts. Lower-income households receive enhanced standardized payments; all tenants receive at least RSO or JCO amounts within 15 days. Tenants also get rights to remain up to 6 months before construction, to return if demolition does not proceed, and in some cases a right of first refusal. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: L.A. Ordinance Nos. 188481 and 188482 (Resident Protections Ordinance).

Source: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (L.A. Mun. Code).

Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(1)(b), as amended by St. 2025, c. 9, §§ 54-55.

A real estate broker or salesperson may contract only with the prospective tenant or only with the landlord (or landlord's agent), and any fee may be paid only by the party who originally hired the broker. Landlords cannot pass the fee of a broker they hired on to tenants. Only licensed brokers or salespersons may charge a fee for finding rental housing. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 112, § 87DDD½ (as amended by St. 2025, c. 9, § 43).

Either party may end a tenancy at will with written notice of three months, or, if rent is paid more often than every three months, notice equal to the rental period or 30 days, whichever is longer; no reason for ending the tenancy is required. For nonpayment of rent, a landlord may end the tenancy with a 14-day written notice to quit, but a tenant who has not received such a notice in the prior 12 months can stop the termination by paying all rent due within 10 days. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 186, § 12.

A written notice to quit for nonpayment of rent to a residential tenant must come with a state form. The form must document any repayment agreements, give information on rental assistance, court rules and legal limits on evictions, and prominently state that the notice is not an eviction. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 31.

Anyone offering rental housing may not discriminate against a person because they receive public assistance or a housing subsidy, such as a rental voucher, or because of any requirement of that assistance or subsidy program. Ads for covered rental housing also may not state a preference or limit based on public assistance recipiency. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 151B, § 4(10).

A landlord may not require a security deposit greater than the first month's rent. The deposit must be held in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account, receipted, accompanied by a statement of condition, earn interest for the tenant, and be returned (less lawful itemized deductions) within 30 days after the tenancy ends. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B.

A0047.explanation: Landlords may not use algorithmic rent coordination services. The ban is enforced both by the city and through private lawsuits. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Jersey City Code § 218-12.

Jersey City regulates rent increases under its Rent Control Ordinance, which the Office of Landlord/Tenant Relations administers and enforces. Properties with 1 to 4 units are exempt. Landlords seeking increases beyond the regulated amount must apply, for example for capital improvements or hardship. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Jersey City Mun. Code Ch. 260.

A landlord or its agent may not charge an application or similar fee above $50 to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental unit. Starting January 1 of the year after enactment, the cap is adjusted each year for inflation (CPI-U, NY-Northern NJ-Long Island) and published by the Division of Consumer Affairs. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-18.1 (P.L. 2025, c.405).

A residential landlord may not evict a tenant, or refuse to renew a written or oral lease, without one of the statutory good causes. Each cause, except nonpayment of rent, requires a written Notice to Quit. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1.

There is no state rent cap, but a rent increase must not be unconscionable and must follow any municipal rent ordinance. Rent cannot be raised mid-lease; a tenant can be evicted for not paying an increase only after a valid notice to quit and notice of rent increase. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(f).

Housing providers may not ask about an applicant's criminal record, orally, in writing or on an application, until after making a conditional offer. They may never consider arrests without conviction, expunged, pardoned, vacated, juvenile or sealed records. After the offer they may consider only listed serious convictions and convictions within look-back periods (6 years first degree, 4 years second/third degree, 1 year fourth degree). They may withdraw an offer only after an individualized assessment showing a substantial, legitimate, nondiscriminatory interest, with written reasons and a chance to appeal. The act also bars requiring drug or alcohol tests. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-52 to 46:8-64 (P.L. 2021, c.110).

Landlords may not discriminate in housing based on the source of lawful income or the source of lawful rent payment a tenant uses. For example, a landlord cannot deny a Section 8 voucher holder an apartment based solely on that source of income. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: New Jersey Law Against Discrimination, N.J.S.A. 10:5-1 et seq..

A landlord may not collect a security deposit greater than one and one-half times one month's rent. Prepaid rent, including last month's rent, counts toward this limit. The deposit must be returned with interest, less itemized deductions, within 30 days after the tenancy ends. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2.

The act this section belongs to (L.1967, c. 265) applies to all rental premises or units used as dwellings. The one exception is owner-occupied premises with no more than two rental units, and only where the tenant has not given the landlord 30 days' written notice invoking the act. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-26.

A0048.explanation: A landlord or foreclosing owner who plans to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources together with the Notice to Quit or notice of lease non-renewal. The landlord must also send a copy of the Notice to Quit or Non-renewal, with a Certificate of Compliance/Service, to the City's Office of Housing Stability. This is a notice requirement; it does not limit the reasons a landlord may end a tenancy. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Boston Housing Stability Notification Act, City of Boston Ordinances Sec. 10-11.7.
Coverage depends on government subsidized, which the public records do not include. Source: Boston Department of Neighborhood Development, Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (Feb. 2017).

In Boston, landlords may not discriminate against renters because they use rental assistance, such as Section 8, social security disability or veterans vouchers. Refusing to accept rental assistance is an example of illegal housing discrimination. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: City of Boston fair housing law, enforced by the Boston Fair Housing Commission.
Proposed, not law. Would cover this building if enacted. Source: Mass. H.5222 (194th General Court).
Proposed, not law. Would cover this building if enacted. Source: Mass. S.2983 (194th General Court).
Proposed, not law. Would cover this building if enacted. Source: Massachusetts House and Senate bills (bill numbers not stated).

Only licensed brokers may charge prospective tenants fees for finding housing, and the broker must give the applicant written notice of the fee amount, time and manner of payment, and whether it depends on a lease being signed, at the first personal meeting. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: 254 CMR 7.

A0049.explanation: Landlords renting any residential dwelling unit in Hoboken may not use software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms that collect and analyze nonpublic competitor information to coordinate, recommend or implement rents, lease terms or occupancy levels among competing lessors. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Hoboken City Code § 158-2 (Ord. No. B-781).

This is not a cap on rent increases. A landlord who raises rent by more than 10% year over year on a lease renewal with a current tenant must first give certain disclosures, either on the first page of the renewal lease or on a Division of Housing form. The disclosures are an itemization of the costs behind the increase, whether a rent algorithm was used, the tenant's right to sue over an unconscionable or unlawful increase, and Division of Housing contact information. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Hoboken City Code § 158-1 (Ord. No. B-750).

Rents in covered Hoboken dwellings are controlled at the October 1, 1985 base rent level. At lease expiration or termination of a periodic tenancy, a landlord may not request or receive an increase greater than 5% or the CPI change, whichever is less, and no more than one such increase is allowed in any 12-month period. Increases above this are void. Separate Board-approved surcharges (tax, water/sewer, capital improvement) and hardship increases are allowed. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Hoboken City Code §§ 155-3, 155-4, 155-5.
Coverage depends on year built, which the public records do not include. Source: Hoboken City Code §§ 155-31 to 155-34.

A landlord or its agent may not charge an application or similar fee above $50 to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental unit. Starting January 1 of the year after enactment, the cap is adjusted each year for inflation (CPI-U, NY-Northern NJ-Long Island) and published by the Division of Consumer Affairs. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-18.1 (P.L. 2025, c.405).

Source: N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(f).
Coverage depends on year built, which the public records do not include. Source: N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5.

For example, a landlord cannot deny a Section 8 voucher holder an apartment based solely on that source of income. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: New Jersey Law Against Discrimination, N.J.S.A. 10:5-1 et seq..

A landlord may not collect a security deposit greater than one and one-half times one month's rent. Prepaid rent, including last month's rent, counts toward this limit. The deposit must be returned with interest, less itemized deductions, within 30 days after the tenancy ends. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2.

The act this section belongs to (L.1967, c. 265) applies to all rental premises or units used as dwellings. The one exception is owner-occupied premises with no more than two rental units, and only where the tenant has not given the landlord 30 days' written notice invoking the act. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-26.

A0050.explanation: No person may use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (software or other method used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set or influence a price or commercial term) as part of a contract, combination or conspiracy to restrain trade. No person may use or distribute such an algorithm while coercing another person to adopt its recommended price or terms. The law covers all products and services, not only rental housing. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729.

A landlord may charge a rental applicant a screening fee no greater than actual out-of-pocket screening costs, and never more than $30 per applicant (adjustable annually by CPI since January 1, 1998). The landlord may collect the fee only when a unit is or will soon be available and only if it offers either a first-come, first-qualified screening process or a full refund to applicants not selected. The landlord must also give an itemized receipt, return unused amounts and provide a copy of the credit report. The current text reflects the amendment by Stats. 2025, Ch. 67 (AB 1170), effective January 1, 2026. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6.
Coverage depends on tenancy months, owner occupied, owner is corporation, government subsidized, which the public records do not include. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2.

For temporary capital improvement evictions lasting less than 20 days, relocation payments are governed by California Civil Code Section 1947.9 rather than the San Francisco Rent Ordinance. For notices served 3/01/26–2/28/27, the amount is $446 per day per tenant household plus actual moving expenses. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9.

Lower-income households (80% AMI or below) displaced by demolition of their units for replacement with new construction must receive relocation benefits consistent with those public entities must pay under Government Code Section 7260 et seq. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 66300.6(b)(4)(A).
Coverage depends on government subsidized, owner is corporation, owner occupied, which the public records do not include. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12.

Landlords may not use the credit history of an applicant who has a government rental subsidy, such as Section 8, unless they offer the applicant the option to provide alternative evidence of a verifiable lawful means to pay their portion of the rent. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955 (SB 267).

Housing providers may check criminal history but may not consider arrests that did not lead to a conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and may not have blanket bans on people with criminal history. A denial based on a conviction must be directly related to tenancy and safety, considering the nature and severity of the crime and the time passed. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA), Cal. Gov. Code § 12900 et seq..

Housing providers may not discriminate against applicants or tenants based on how they will pay rent (source of income). This includes Housing Choice (Section 8) vouchers and other rental assistance. Providers may not refuse to comply with subsidy program requirements, apply different terms such as higher deposits, or advertise 'No Section 8.' Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA), Cal. Gov. Code § 12900 et seq..

A landlord may not demand or receive security, however named, of more than one month's rent on top of the first month's rent. Small landlords who are natural persons (or LLCs of natural persons) owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units in total may charge up to two months' rent, except to service members. The landlord must return the deposit with an itemized statement within 21 days after move-out, and may not call any part of it nonrefundable. The section was last amended by AB 414 (Stats. 2025, Ch. 340), effective January 1, 2026. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5.

Bans selling or using algorithmic devices that analyze nonpublic competitor rental data to recommend rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco. A tenant or the City Attorney may sue a violator. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.10C.

A landlord may evict a tenant from a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance only for one of 17 listed just cause reasons, and that reason must be the dominant motive for the eviction. The end of a lease or a change in ownership alone is not just cause. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9(a).

Landlords who evict tenants under the Ellis Act (withdrawal of units from the rental market) must pay relocation. For notices served 3/01/26 to 2/28/27 it is $11,110.05 per tenant, up to $33,330.13 per unit, plus $7,443.90 for each elderly (62+) or disabled tenant. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9A(e).

Landlords who evict for owner/relative move-in, demolition or permanent removal from housing use, temporary capital improvement work, or substantial rehabilitation must pay relocation. The amount depends on the date the eviction notice is served. For notices served 3/01/26 to 2/28/27 it is $8,245.00 per tenant, up to $24,733.00 per unit, plus $5,497.00 for each elderly (60+) or disabled tenant or household with minor children. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9C.

For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable rent increase effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6% of the tenant's base rent. The prior period's (March 1, 2025 to February 28, 2026) allowable increase was 1.4%. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code ch. 37 (Residential Rent Stabilization and Arbitration Ordinance), annual allowable increase.
Coverage depends on government subsidized, which the public records do not include. Source: San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

Landlords must pay interest on security deposits at the Rent Board rate of 4.2% for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027. Earlier periods used 5.0% (2025–26) and 5.2% (2024–25). Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code Ch. 49 (Security Deposit Interest).

Only licensed brokers may charge prospective tenants fees for finding housing, and the broker must give the applicant written notice of the fee amount, time and manner of payment, and whether it depends on a lease being signed, at the first personal meeting. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: 254 CMR 7.

At or before the start of a tenancy, a landlord or the landlord's agent may not require a tenant or applicant to pay the landlord or its agent anything beyond first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit of up to one month's rent, and the cost of buying and installing a key and lock. The 2025 amendment, effective August 1, 2025, extended the limit to the lessor's agents and payments to them; earlier text applied only to lessors. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(1)(b), as amended by St. 2025, c. 9, §§ 54-55.

A real estate broker or salesperson may contract only with the prospective tenant or only with the landlord (or landlord's agent), and any fee may be paid only by the party who originally hired the broker. Landlords cannot pass the fee of a broker they hired on to tenants. Only licensed brokers or salespersons may charge a fee for finding rental housing. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 112, § 87DDD½ (as amended by St. 2025, c. 9, § 43).

Either party may end a tenancy at will with written notice of three months, or, if rent is paid more often than every three months, notice equal to the rental period or 30 days, whichever is longer; no reason for ending the tenancy is required. For nonpayment of rent, a landlord may end the tenancy with a 14-day written notice to quit, but a tenant who has not received such a notice in the prior 12 months can stop the termination by paying all rent due within 10 days. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 186, § 12.

A written notice to quit for nonpayment of rent to a residential tenant must come with a state form. The form must document any repayment agreements, give information on rental assistance, court rules and legal limits on evictions, and prominently state that the notice is not an eviction. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 31.

Anyone offering rental housing may not discriminate against a person because they receive public assistance or a housing subsidy, such as a rental voucher, or because of any requirement of that assistance or subsidy program. Ads for covered rental housing also may not state a preference or limit based on public assistance recipiency. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 151B, § 4(10).

A landlord may not require a security deposit greater than the first month's rent. The deposit must be held in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account, receipted, accompanied by a statement of condition, earn interest for the tenant, and be returned (less lawful itemized deductions) within 30 days after the tenancy ends. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B.

A0054.explanation: A landlord or foreclosing owner who plans to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources together with the Notice to Quit or notice of lease non-renewal. The landlord must also send a copy of the Notice to Quit or Non-renewal, with a Certificate of Compliance/Service, to the City's Office of Housing Stability. This is a notice requirement; it does not limit the reasons a landlord may end a tenancy. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Boston Housing Stability Notification Act, City of Boston Ordinances Sec. 10-11.7.
Coverage depends on government subsidized, which the public records do not include. Source: Boston Department of Neighborhood Development, Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (Feb. 2017).

Source: City of Boston fair housing law, enforced by the Boston Fair Housing Commission.

A0055.explanation: No person may use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (software or other method used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set or influence a price or commercial term) as part of a contract, combination or conspiracy to restrain trade. No person may use or distribute such an algorithm while coercing another person to adopt its recommended price or terms. The law covers all products and services, not only rental housing. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729.

A landlord may charge a rental applicant a screening fee no greater than actual out-of-pocket screening costs, and never more than $30 per applicant (adjustable annually by CPI since January 1, 1998). The landlord may collect the fee only when a unit is or will soon be available and only if it offers either a first-come, first-qualified screening process or a full refund to applicants not selected. The landlord must also give an itemized receipt, return unused amounts and provide a copy of the credit report. The current text reflects the amendment by Stats. 2025, Ch. 67 (AB 1170), effective January 1, 2026. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6.
Coverage depends on tenancy months, owner occupied, owner is corporation, government subsidized, which the public records do not include. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2.

For temporary capital improvement evictions lasting less than 20 days, relocation payments are governed by California Civil Code Section 1947.9 rather than the San Francisco Rent Ordinance. For notices served 3/01/26–2/28/27, the amount is $446 per day per tenant household plus actual moving expenses. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9.

Lower-income households (80% AMI or below) displaced by demolition of their units for replacement with new construction must receive relocation benefits consistent with those public entities must pay under Government Code Section 7260 et seq. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 66300.6(b)(4)(A).
Coverage depends on government subsidized, owner is corporation, owner occupied, which the public records do not include. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12.

Landlords may not use the credit history of an applicant who has a government rental subsidy, such as Section 8, unless they offer the applicant the option to provide alternative evidence of a verifiable lawful means to pay their portion of the rent. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955 (SB 267).

Housing providers may check criminal history but may not consider arrests that did not lead to a conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and may not have blanket bans on people with criminal history. A denial based on a conviction must be directly related to tenancy and safety, considering the nature and severity of the crime and the time passed. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA), Cal. Gov. Code § 12900 et seq..

Housing providers may not discriminate against applicants or tenants based on how they will pay rent (source of income). This includes Housing Choice (Section 8) vouchers and other rental assistance. Providers may not refuse to comply with subsidy program requirements, apply different terms such as higher deposits, or advertise 'No Section 8.' Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA), Cal. Gov. Code § 12900 et seq..

A landlord may not demand or receive security, however named, of more than one month's rent on top of the first month's rent. Small landlords who are natural persons (or LLCs of natural persons) owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units in total may charge up to two months' rent, except to service members. The landlord must return the deposit with an itemized statement within 21 days after move-out, and may not call any part of it nonrefundable. The section was last amended by AB 414 (Stats. 2025, Ch. 340), effective January 1, 2026. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5.

Bans selling or using algorithmic devices that analyze nonpublic competitor rental data to recommend rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco. A tenant or the City Attorney may sue a violator. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.10C.

A landlord may evict a tenant from a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance only for one of 17 listed just cause reasons, and that reason must be the dominant motive for the eviction. The end of a lease or a change in ownership alone is not just cause. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9(a).

Landlords who evict tenants under the Ellis Act (withdrawal of units from the rental market) must pay relocation. For notices served 3/01/26 to 2/28/27 it is $11,110.05 per tenant, up to $33,330.13 per unit, plus $7,443.90 for each elderly (62+) or disabled tenant. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9A(e).

Landlords who evict for owner/relative move-in, demolition or permanent removal from housing use, temporary capital improvement work, or substantial rehabilitation must pay relocation. The amount depends on the date the eviction notice is served. For notices served 3/01/26 to 2/28/27 it is $8,245.00 per tenant, up to $24,733.00 per unit, plus $5,497.00 for each elderly (60+) or disabled tenant or household with minor children. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9C.

For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable rent increase effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6% of the tenant's base rent. The prior period's (March 1, 2025 to February 28, 2026) allowable increase was 1.4%. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code ch. 37 (Residential Rent Stabilization and Arbitration Ordinance), annual allowable increase.
Coverage depends on government subsidized, which the public records do not include. Source: San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

Landlords must pay interest on security deposits at the Rent Board rate of 4.2% for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027. Earlier periods used 5.0% (2025–26) and 5.2% (2024–25). Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code Ch. 49 (Security Deposit Interest).

A denial based on a conviction must be directly related to tenancy and safety, considering the nature and severity of the crime and the time passed. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA), Cal. Gov. Code § 12900 et seq..

Housing providers may not discriminate against applicants or tenants based on how they will pay rent (source of income). This includes Housing Choice (Section 8) vouchers and other rental assistance. Providers may not refuse to comply with subsidy program requirements, apply different terms such as higher deposits, or advertise 'No Section 8.' Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA), Cal. Gov. Code § 12900 et seq..

A landlord may not demand or receive security, however named, of more than one month's rent on top of the first month's rent. Small landlords who are natural persons (or LLCs of natural persons) owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units in total may charge up to two months' rent, except to service members. The landlord must return the deposit with an itemized statement within 21 days after move-out, and may not call any part of it nonrefundable. The section was last amended by AB 414 (Stats. 2025, Ch. 340), effective January 1, 2026. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5.
Proposed, not law. Would cover this building if enacted. Source: L.A. City Council File No. 24-1031 (Motion, Sept. 3, 2024).

A landlord may evict an RSO tenant only for listed at-fault reasons (such as nonpayment, lease violation, nuisance, or illegal use) or no-fault reasons (such as owner or family move-in, resident manager, demolition, government order, or conversion to affordable housing). No-fault evictions require tenant relocation assistance, and every termination notice must be filed with LAHD within three business days of service. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: L.A. Mun. Code § 151.09.

Owners who demolish a Protected Unit for new construction must pay relocation under one of three options, paying the higher of State (Housing Crisis Act) or City amounts. Lower-income households receive enhanced standardized payments; all tenants receive at least RSO or JCO amounts within 15 days. Tenants also get rights to remain up to 6 months before construction, to return if demolition does not proceed, and in some cases a right of first refusal. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: L.A. Ordinance Nos. 188481 and 188482 (Resident Protections Ordinance).

Landlords of covered rental units in the City of Los Angeles may not end a tenancy without one of the listed just causes. For no-fault reasons (such as owner move-in, demolition or removal from the rental market), the landlord must pay relocation assistance. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (L.A. Mun. Code).

The RSO requires landlords of RSO units to pay interest on tenants' security deposits. This page does not state the rate or timing. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: L.A. Mun. Code § 151.00 et seq. (Rent Stabilization Ordinance).

A0061.explanation: No person may use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (software or other method used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set or influence a price or commercial term) as part of a contract, combination or conspiracy to restrain trade. No person may use or distribute such an algorithm while coercing another person to adopt its recommended price or terms. The law covers all products and services, not only rental housing. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729.

A landlord may charge a rental applicant a screening fee no greater than actual out-of-pocket screening costs, and never more than $30 per applicant (adjustable annually by CPI since January 1, 1998). The landlord may collect the fee only when a unit is or will soon be available and only if it offers either a first-come, first-qualified screening process or a full refund to applicants not selected. The landlord must also give an itemized receipt, return unused amounts and provide a copy of the credit report. The current text reflects the amendment by Stats. 2025, Ch. 67 (AB 1170), effective January 1, 2026. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6.
Coverage depends on tenancy months, owner occupied, owner is corporation, government subsidized, which the public records do not include. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2.

For temporary capital improvement evictions lasting less than 20 days, relocation payments are governed by California Civil Code Section 1947.9 rather than the San Francisco Rent Ordinance. For notices served 3/01/26–2/28/27, the amount is $446 per day per tenant household plus actual moving expenses. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9.

Lower-income households (80% AMI or below) displaced by demolition of their units for replacement with new construction must receive relocation benefits consistent with those public entities must pay under Government Code Section 7260 et seq. A tenant or the City Attorney may sue a violator. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.10C.

A landlord may evict a tenant from a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance only for one of 17 listed just cause reasons, and that reason must be the dominant motive for the eviction. The end of a lease or a change in ownership alone is not just cause. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9(a).

Landlords who evict tenants under the Ellis Act (withdrawal of units from the rental market) must pay relocation. For notices served 3/01/26 to 2/28/27 it is $11,110.05 per tenant, up to $33,330.13 per unit, plus $7,443.90 for each elderly (62+) or disabled tenant. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9A(e).

Landlords who evict for owner/relative move-in, demolition or permanent removal from housing use, temporary capital improvement work, or substantial rehabilitation must pay relocation. The amount depends on the date the eviction notice is served. For notices served 3/01/26 to 2/28/27 it is $8,245.00 per tenant, up to $24,733.00 per unit, plus $5,497.00 for each elderly (60+) or disabled tenant or household with minor children. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9C.

For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable rent increase effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6% of the tenant's base rent. The prior period's (March 1, 2025 to February 28, 2026) allowable increase was 1.4%. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code ch. 37 (Residential Rent Stabilization and Arbitration Ordinance), annual allowable increase.

The landlord must also send a copy of the Notice to Quit or Non-renewal, with a Certificate of Compliance/Service, to the City's Office of Housing Stability. This is a notice requirement; it does not limit the reasons a landlord may end a tenancy. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Boston Housing Stability Notification Act, City of Boston Ordinances Sec. 10-11.7.
Coverage depends on government subsidized, which the public records do not include. Source: Boston Department of Neighborhood Development, Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (Feb. 2017).

Only licensed brokers may charge prospective tenants fees for finding housing, and the broker must give the applicant written notice of the fee amount, time and manner of payment, and whether it depends on a lease being signed, at the first personal meeting. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: 254 CMR 7.

At or before the start of a tenancy, a landlord or the landlord's agent may not require a tenant or applicant to pay the landlord or its agent anything beyond first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit of up to one month's rent, and the cost of buying and installing a key and lock. The 2025 amendment, effective August 1, 2025, extended the limit to the lessor's agents and payments to them; earlier text applied only to lessors. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(1)(b), as amended by St. 2025, c. 9, §§ 54-55.

A real estate broker or salesperson may contract only with the prospective tenant or only with the landlord (or landlord's agent), and any fee may be paid only by the party who originally hired the broker. Landlords cannot pass the fee of a broker they hired on to tenants. Only licensed brokers or salespersons may charge a fee for finding rental housing. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 112, § 87DDD½ (as amended by St. 2025, c. 9, § 43).

Either party may end a tenancy at will with written notice of three months, or, if rent is paid more often than every three months, notice equal to the rental period or 30 days, whichever is longer; no reason for ending the tenancy is required. For nonpayment of rent, a landlord may end the tenancy with a 14-day written notice to quit, but a tenant who has not received such a notice in the prior 12 months can stop the termination by paying all rent due within 10 days. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 186, § 12.

A written notice to quit for nonpayment of rent to a residential tenant must come with a state form. The form must document any repayment agreements, give information on rental assistance, court rules and legal limits on evictions, and prominently state that the notice is not an eviction. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 31.

Anyone offering rental housing may not discriminate against a person because they receive public assistance or a housing subsidy, such as a rental voucher, or because of any requirement of that assistance or subsidy program. A landlord may not require a security deposit greater than the first month's rent. The deposit must be held in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account, receipted, accompanied by a statement of condition, earn interest for the tenant, and be returned (less lawful itemized deductions) within 30 days after the tenancy ends. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B.

Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 66300.6(b)(4)(A).
Coverage depends on government subsidized, owner is corporation, owner occupied, which the public records do not include. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12.

Landlords may not use the credit history of an applicant who has a government rental subsidy, such as Section 8, unless they offer the applicant the option to provide alternative evidence of a verifiable lawful means to pay their portion of the rent. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955 (SB 267).

Housing providers may check criminal history but may not consider arrests that did not lead to a conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and may not have blanket bans on people with criminal history. A denial based on a conviction must be directly related to tenancy and safety, considering the nature and severity of the crime and the time passed. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA), Cal. Gov. Code § 12900 et seq..

Housing providers may not discriminate against applicants or tenants based on how they will pay rent (source of income). This includes Housing Choice (Section 8) vouchers and other rental assistance. Providers may not refuse to comply with subsidy program requirements, apply different terms such as higher deposits, or advertise 'No Section 8.' Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA), Cal. Gov. Code § 12900 et seq..

A landlord may not demand or receive security, however named, of more than one month's rent on top of the first month's rent. Small landlords who are natural persons (or LLCs of natural persons) owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units in total may charge up to two months' rent, except to service members. The landlord must return the deposit with an itemized statement within 21 days after move-out, and may not call any part of it nonrefundable. The section was last amended by AB 414 (Stats. 2025, Ch. 340), effective January 1, 2026. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5.
Proposed, not law. Would cover this building if enacted. Source: L.A. City Council File No. 24-1031 (Motion, Sept. 3, 2024).

Owners who demolish a Protected Unit for new construction must pay relocation under one of three options, paying the higher of State (Housing Crisis Act) or City amounts. Lower-income households receive enhanced standardized payments; all tenants receive at least RSO or JCO amounts within 15 days. Tenants also get rights to remain up to 6 months before construction, to return if demolition does not proceed, and in some cases a right of first refusal. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: L.A. Ordinance Nos. 188481 and 188482 (Resident Protections Ordinance).

Landlords of covered rental units in the City of Los Angeles may not end a tenancy without one of the listed just causes. For no-fault reasons (such as owner move-in, demolition or removal from the rental market), the landlord must pay relocation assistance. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (L.A. Mun. Code).

A0067.explanation: No person may use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (software or other method used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set or influence a price or commercial term) as part of a contract, combination or conspiracy to restrain trade. No person may use or distribute such an algorithm while coercing another person to adopt its recommended price or terms. The law covers all products and services, not only rental housing. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729.

A landlord may charge a rental applicant a screening fee no greater than actual out-of-pocket screening costs, and never more than $30 per applicant (adjustable annually by CPI since January 1, 1998). The landlord may collect the fee only when a unit is or will soon be available and only if it offers either a first-come, first-qualified screening process or a full refund to applicants not selected. The landlord must also give an itemized receipt, return unused amounts and provide a copy of the credit report. The current text reflects the amendment by Stats. 2025, Ch. 67 (AB 1170), effective January 1, 2026. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6.
Coverage depends on tenancy months, owner occupied, owner is corporation, government subsidized, which the public records do not include. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2.

For temporary capital improvement evictions lasting less than 20 days, relocation payments are governed by California Civil Code Section 1947.9 rather than the San Francisco Rent Ordinance. For notices served 3/01/26–2/28/27, the amount is $446 per day per tenant household plus actual moving expenses. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9.

No-fault evictions require tenant relocation assistance, and every termination notice must be filed with LAHD within three business days of service. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: L.A. Mun. Code § 151.09.

The RSO requires landlords of RSO units to pay interest on tenants' security deposits. This page does not state the rate or timing. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: L.A. Mun. Code § 151.00 et seq. (Rent Stabilization Ordinance).

A0068.explanation: A landlord or foreclosing owner who plans to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources together with the Notice to Quit or notice of lease non-renewal. The landlord must also send a copy of the Notice to Quit or Non-renewal, with a Certificate of Compliance/Service, to the City's Office of Housing Stability. This is a notice requirement; it does not limit the reasons a landlord may end a tenancy. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Boston Housing Stability Notification Act, City of Boston Ordinances Sec. 10-11.7.
Coverage depends on government subsidized, which the public records do not include. Source: Boston Department of Neighborhood Development, Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (Feb. 2017).

In Boston, landlords may not discriminate against renters because they use rental assistance, such as Section 8, social security disability or veterans vouchers. Refusing to accept rental assistance is an example of illegal housing discrimination. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: City of Boston fair housing law, enforced by the Boston Fair Housing Commission.
Proposed, not law. Would cover this building if enacted. Source: Mass. H.5222 (194th General Court).
Proposed, not law. Would cover this building if enacted. Source: Mass. S.2983 (194th General Court).
Proposed, not law. Would cover this building if enacted. Source: Massachusetts House and Senate bills (bill numbers not stated).

Only licensed brokers may charge prospective tenants fees for finding housing, and the broker must give the applicant written notice of the fee amount, time and manner of payment, and whether it depends on a lease being signed, at the first personal meeting. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: 254 CMR 7.

At or before the start of a tenancy, a landlord or the landlord's agent may not require a tenant or applicant to pay the landlord or its agent anything beyond first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit of up to one month's rent, and the cost of buying and installing a key and lock. The 2025 amendment, effective August 1, 2025, extended the limit to the lessor's agents and payments to them; earlier text applied only to lessors. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(1)(b), as amended by St. 2025, c. 9, §§ 54-55.

A real estate broker or salesperson may contract only with the prospective tenant or only with the landlord (or landlord's agent), and any fee may be paid only by the party who originally hired the broker. Landlords cannot pass the fee of a broker they hired on to tenants. Only licensed brokers or salespersons may charge a fee for finding rental housing. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 112, § 87DDD½ (as amended by St. 2025, c. 9, § 43).

Either party may end a tenancy at will with written notice of three months, or, if rent is paid more often than every three months, notice equal to the rental period or 30 days, whichever is longer; no reason for ending the tenancy is required. For nonpayment of rent, a landlord may end the tenancy with a 14-day written notice to quit, but a tenant who has not received such a notice in the prior 12 months can stop the termination by paying all rent due within 10 days. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 186, § 12.

A written notice to quit for nonpayment of rent to a residential tenant must come with a state form. The form must document any repayment agreements, give information on rental assistance, court rules and legal limits on evictions, and prominently state that the notice is not an eviction. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 31.

Anyone offering rental housing may not discriminate against a person because they receive public assistance or a housing subsidy, such as a rental voucher, or because of any requirement of that assistance or subsidy program. Ads for covered rental housing also may not state a preference or limit based on public assistance recipiency. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 151B, § 4(10).

A landlord may not require a security deposit greater than the first month's rent. The deposit must be held in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account, receipted, accompanied by a statement of condition, earn interest for the tenant, and be returned (less lawful itemized deductions) within 30 days after the tenancy ends. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B.

Bans selling or using algorithmic devices that analyze nonpublic competitor rental data to recommend rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco. A tenant or the City Attorney may sue a violator. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.10C.

A landlord may evict a tenant from a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance only for one of 17 listed just cause reasons, and that reason must be the dominant motive for the eviction. The end of a lease or a change in ownership alone is not just cause. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9(a).

Landlords who evict tenants under the Ellis Act (withdrawal of units from the rental market) must pay relocation. For notices served 3/01/26 to 2/28/27 it is $11,110.05 per tenant, up to $33,330.13 per unit, plus $7,443.90 for each elderly (62+) or disabled tenant. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9A(e).

Landlords who evict for owner/relative move-in, demolition or permanent removal from housing use, temporary capital improvement work, or substantial rehabilitation must pay relocation. The amount depends on the date the eviction notice is served. For notices served 3/01/26 to 2/28/27 it is $8,245.00 per tenant, up to $24,733.00 per unit, plus $5,497.00 for each elderly (60+) or disabled tenant or household with minor children. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9C.

For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable rent increase effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6% of the tenant's base rent. The prior period's (March 1, 2025 to February 28, 2026) allowable increase was 1.4%. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code ch. 37 (Residential Rent Stabilization and Arbitration Ordinance), annual allowable increase.
Coverage depends on government subsidized, which the public records do not include. Source: San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

Landlords must pay interest on security deposits at the Rent Board rate of 4.2% for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027. Earlier periods used 5.0% (2025–26) and 5.2% (2024–25). Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code Ch. 49 (Security Deposit Interest).
